signOffConditionVerdicts.note: Four facts carry all seven attributes. Two carry six and record the enumeration members as an explicit exception, which is the mechanism for an attribute that is genuinely unsettled rather than omitted; the other six attributes are stated in the entry so nothing is lost. The scope is payload and power only, because the product group is PLACEHOLDER in the telemetry ICD and the autonomy group waits on DG-AUT, so declaring facts there would name values the aircraft will never send.

All six Aerora fact groups remain created at vehicle construction and this record creates none dynamically. Carrying no fact is not the same as not existing: the four groups this record declares no fact for are still constructed, so the telemetry record column header stays stable and no group appears later to shift every subsequent column. That is R-027 and AERORA-GCS-REQ-022.

Each vehicle receives its own fact-group instances through AeroraVehicleFactGroupRegistrar, one registrar per vehicle, which is the ADR-016 attachment the core-edit part authorises. Nothing in this record routes through FirmwarePlugin::factGroups(), which is the competing path that hands one cached set to every vehicle of a firmware class and is the R4-001 defect itself.

guardPermissions.reason: Both parts the register records as permitting this guard are now accepted, so the recorded value may move to true and an assertion may be added. The registration path is settled and the ADR-016 core edit is authorised, so the privileged call compiles and the registrar can register. The six fact groups are still constructor-time, so permitting registration does not permit a dynamic group.

entries.value: Declared as a fact with an unsettled enumeration. Six of the seven attributes are known: the fact name is sprayGateState, it carries no unit because it is an enumeration, its value range is the int32 range NAMED_VALUE_INT carries, its owning fact group is Aerora payload, its freshness class is System, and its inbound message is NAMED_VALUE_INT with the name field aeSprayGt. Only the member set is unsettled: the interlock is a Stateflow chart and the archive does not enumerate its states. Recorded as an exception rather than guessed, because with NAMED_VALUE_INT the integer is what travels, so a guessed member becomes permanent in every flight log the first time firmware sends it. Appending members later is safe; renumbering silently rewrites records already on disk.

Declared as a fact with an unsettled enumeration, on the same terms. The fact name is tetherMode, no unit because it is an enumeration, the int32 range NAMED_VALUE_INT carries, owning fact group Aerora power, freshness class System, inbound message NAMED_VALUE_INT with the name field aeTethMode. The model carries TETHER_MODE beside AUTO_MAX_VEL, AUTO_ALT_MIN_M and AUTO_SP_TIMEOUT_S, which implies an AUTO mode without enumerating the set, so the members stay unsettled rather than inferred from neighbouring parameter names. The owner has since stated that the aircraft runs tether supply normally and switches to onboard battery where the tether cannot reach, with an automatic hardware failover on tether loss, so at least two modes exist; the integers they travel as are still unsettled and are what this exception holds.
